correctness.rationale: The cactus cycle-vertex incidence forest yields linearly independent nonzero cycle relations with no singleton in their span. All cycle infections preserve the quotient-span closure. A minimal outside vertex allegedly in quotient-span closure of a cycle-convex set produces a symmetric-difference witness whose terminal cycle may be pruned from its rooted incidence forest; the last cycle forces the outside vertex, contradiction. Thus entire hull operator equals the loopless binary matroid closure. Linear independence then implies Helly/Radon independence, and the converse to convex independence is elementary. Verified all 15 finite test profiles and 3576 subsets with distinct hull/rank algorithms, recognizing finite checks do not prove the infinite result.

value.rationale: A structural binary-matroid representation for the entire convexity on cacti, including unboundedly many cycles, is substantially stronger than a numeric small-case computation. It unifies three independently motivated cycle-convexity parameters into n−k, explains the role of cactus block topology and supplies an exchange-structured linear closure oracle; this goes beyond the near-extremal classified regimes and has plausible use in convexity optimizations and characterization questions.
